title: Relative Tor amplitude is detected by simultaneous source and base prime localizations
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, let $K^\bullet$ be an arbitrary complex of $A$-modules, and let $a\le b$ be integers. Work in the unbounded derived categories of modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], computing derived tensors by K-flat resolutions [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. For a prime $\mathfrak q\subset A$, put $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap R$ and let $K^\bullet_{\mathfrak q}$ be termwise localization [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], with scalars restricted by the induced map $R_{\mathfrak p}\to A_{\mathfrak q}$. The following are equivalent: (1) $H^i(K^\bullet\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N)=0$ for every $R$-module $N$ in degree zero and every $i\notin[a,b]$; (2) for every prime $\mathfrak q\subset A$, $H^i(K^\bullet_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{R_{\mathfrak p}}^{\mathbf L}L)=0$ for every $R_{\mathfrak p}$-module $L$ in degree zero and every $i\notin[a,b]$. No flatness, finiteness or boundedness assumption on the map or complex is required.

source.place: Tag 0B67, lemma-tor-amplitude-localization, equivalence of (1) and (2), renaming the base A to R and the algebra B to A.

proof.text: Fix an $R$-module $N$, placed in degree zero. By [lem-pc-source-module-kflat-resolution] choose K-flat quasi-isomorphisms $P^\bullet\to N[0]$ and $F^\bullet\to\operatorname{Res}_R K^\bullet$. The tensor-model theorem [lem-pc-source-kflat-module-tensor-model] computes $K^\bullet\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N$ by $\operatorname{Tot}(F^\bullet\otimes_R N[0])$. K-flatness [def-pc-module-kflat-complex] says tensoring on either side preserves quasi-isomorphisms. Since $P^\bullet$ is K-flat, the map $\operatorname{Tot}(F^\bullet\otimes_R P^\bullet)\to\operatorname{Tot}(K^\bullet\otimes_R P^\bullet)$ is a quasi-isomorphism; since $F^\bullet$ is K-flat, the map $\operatorname{Tot}(F^\bullet\otimes_R P^\bullet)\to\operatorname{Tot}(F^\bullet\otimes_R N[0])$ is also one. Hence $C_N^\bullet=\operatorname{Tot}(K^\bullet\otimes_R P^\bullet)$ computes the desired derived tensor. This argument applies to any supplied K-flat resolution of the test module. With the total differential of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], multiplication on the unchanged $K$ factor commutes with both differential terms, making $C_N^\bullet$ and $H^i(C_N^\bullet)$ actual $A$-modules. The auxiliary $F^\bullet$ is resolved over $R$; we never assert that an $A$-K-flat resolution is $R$-K-flat.

source.place: Tag 0B67, proof: H^i is a module over the source algebra; expanded using Tag 06Y4 (lemma-K-flat-resolution) and more-algebra.tex definition-derived-tor and lemma-flip-douoble-tensor-product.

proof.text: For any commutative ring $B$, multiplicative subset $T\subseteq B$ and arbitrary $B$-complex $D^\bullet$, [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] says that termwise localization is exact. It is additive by the fraction formulas, so [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] gives $H^i(T^{-1}D^\bullet)\cong T^{-1}H^i(D^\bullet)$ in every degree. In particular localization preserves quasi-isomorphisms. We will use this first over $R$ with $T=R\setminus\mathfrak p$ and then over $A$ with $T=A\setminus\mathfrak q$; neither application needs a bounded complex.

source.place: Tag 0B67, displayed localization of cohomology; algebra.tex Tag 00CS (proposition-localization-exact) and homology.tex Tag 010N (lemma-exact-functor).

proof.text: Fix a prime $\mathfrak q\subset A$, put $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ for the given map $\varphi:R\to A$, and set $P_{\mathfrak p}^\bullet=R_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_R P^\bullet$. The extension theorem [lem-pc-kflat-extension-of-scalars] makes this complex K-flat over $R_{\mathfrak p}$. Step 2 makes its augmentation to $N_{\mathfrak p}[0]$ a quasi-isomorphism. Here scalar extension equals termwise localization: $(r/t)\otimes u\mapsto ru/t$, with inverse $u/t\mapsto(1/t)\otimes u$, as the tensor and fraction relations verify. Consequently [lem-pc-source-kflat-module-tensor-model], with the two-resolution computation of Step 1 (now over $R_{\mathfrak p}$), computes $K^\bullet_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{R_{\mathfrak p}}^{\mathbf L}N_{\mathfrak p}$ by $\operatorname{Tot}(K^\bullet_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{R_{\mathfrak p}}P^\bullet_{\mathfrak p})$. The map $R_{\mathfrak p}\to A_{\mathfrak q}$ sends $r/t$ to $\varphi(r)/\varphi(t)$; it exists because $t\notin\mathfrak p$ implies $\varphi(t)\notin\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Tag 0B67, displayed tensor over the contracted-prime base localization; omitted forward implication expanded using Tag 06Y1 (lemma-base-change-K-flat).

proof.text: The ordinary tensor complexes in Steps 1 and 3 are related by an explicit $A_{\mathfrak q}$-linear chain isomorphism $$(C_N^\bullet)_{\mathfrak q}\longrightarrow\operatorname{Tot}(K^\bullet_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{R_{\mathfrak p}}P^\bullet_{\mathfrak p}),\qquad (k\otimes u)/s\longmapsto(k/s)\otimes(u/1).$$ Its inverse on a homogeneous generator is $$(k/s)\otimes(u/t)\longmapsto(k\otimes u)/(s\varphi(t)),$$ where $s\notin\mathfrak q$ and $t\notin\mathfrak p$. The fraction relations of [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] and tensor balancing give well-defined maps: moving $r/t$ between the factors multiplies the numerator by $\varphi(r)$ or $r$ and introduces the same denominator $\varphi(t)$. The two composites fix every generator. Apply these formulas to finite sums of homogeneous generators; a common product of denominators puts any such sum over one denominator, so the maps also cover the direct sums in every total degree. Both maps commute separately with $d_K\otimes1$ and $(-1)^r1\otimes d_P$, with the same $r$ before and after localization. Thus they commute with the total differential, including for unbounded complexes.

source.place: Tag 0B67, displayed derived-tensor localization identity: elementary fraction and total-differential verification.

proof.text: Apply cohomology to the chain isomorphism of Step 4, use Step 2 on its left side, and use the tensor models of Steps 1 and 3. This gives, for every $R$-module $N$, prime $\mathfrak q$ and integer $i$, the comparison $$H^i(K^\bullet\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N)_{\mathfrak q}\cong H^i(K^\bullet_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{R_{\mathfrak p}}^{\mathbf L}N_{\mathfrak p}).$$ The left side is localization of the actual $A$-module $H^i(C_N^\bullet)$, and the right side uses the specific structural map $R_{\mathfrak p}\to A_{\mathfrak q}$ of Step 3. This is a combination of the preceding computations, with no change from relative to absolute Tor amplitude.

source.place: Tag 0B67, the cohomology localization identity in its proof.

proof.text: Assume (1), fix $\mathfrak q$, and let $L$ be any $R_{\mathfrak p}$-module. Use $N=L$ by restriction to $R$ in Step 5. Its localization satisfies $N_{\mathfrak p}\cong L$: send $l/t$ to $t^{-1}l$ and send $l$ back to $l/1$; these maps are inverse because each $t\notin\mathfrak p$ already acts invertibly. For $i\notin[a,b]$, assumption (1) makes the left side of Step 5 zero. Its right side, after this module isomorphism, is exactly $H^i(K^\bullet_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{R_{\mathfrak p}}^{\mathbf L}L)$. It is zero. Since $\mathfrak q$ and $L$ were arbitrary, this proves (2), including the implication omitted in the source.

source.place: Tag 0B67, omitted implication (1) implies (2), using restricted localized test modules.

proof.text:
Assume (2), fix $N$ and $i

e x\in H$. Its annihilator $I=\{a\in A:ax=0\}$ is a proper ideal. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal] choose a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\supseteq I$. It is prime: if $uv\in\mathfrak m$ and $u
otin\mathfrak m$, write $1=c+du$ with $c\in\mathfrak m$ and multiply by $v$ to get $v\in\mathfrak m$. As $H_{\mathfrak m}=0$, the fraction criterion of [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] gives $s
otin\mathfrak m$ with $sx=0$, contradicting $s\in I\subseteq\mathfrak m$. Hence $H=0$. All $N$ and all degrees outside the interval were arbitrary, so (1) holds. If $A$ is the zero ring, every $A$-module is zero already; the same argument is vacuous. The zero complex, $a=b$, and the identity ring map cause no exceptional step.
